name: JORDAN ELLIS
headline: Senior Data Engineer | Python · Apache Spark · AWS · Snowflake
summary: Senior Data Engineer with about 12 years of experience building batch and streaming data platforms for media, telecom, logistics, banking and healthcare teams. Designs pipelines in **Python** and **Apache Spark** on **AWS**, streams events through **Kafka**, and models analytics-ready data in **Snowflake** with **dbt**. Runs production workflows in **Apache Airflow** with data-quality gates, automates infrastructure with **Terraform**, and ships changes through CI/CD with tests on every merge. Earlier work on **Teradata**, **Informatica PowerCenter** and **Oracle** grounds strong SQL and dimensional modeling skills. Known for clear runbooks, steady production support and close work with the analysts who depend on the data each morning.
skills: Apache Spark, PySpark, Kafka, AWS Glue, Informatica PowerCenter
AWS, S3, EMR, Azure, Azure Blob Storage
Snowflake, Redshift, Teradata, Oracle, SQL Server, dbt, dimensional modeling
Terraform, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Docker, Git, CI/CD

employers.header: Contoso Media | Senior Data Engineer | Feb 2023 - Present
employers.usecase: A streaming analytics platform on AWS turns playback, ad and subscription events into reporting for content, marketing and finance teams. The data team works in two-week sprints with product analysts, balancing new data products against strict morning delivery deadlines.
bullets: Design batch and streaming pipelines in Apache Spark on AWS EMR that process viewing events for recommendation and royalty reporting teams.
Built a Kafka ingestion layer that lands playback and ad events in S3 within minutes, replacing nightly file drops so content teams see audience trends the same day.
Model subscriber, title and viewing facts in Snowflake with dbt, publishing tested marts that finance and marketing analysts query directly.
Orchestrate daily content, ads and finance workflows in Apache Airflow with retries, data-quality gates and SLA alerts, cutting the manual reruns the on-call engineer used to make each morning.
Tuned Spark joins and partitioning to shorten the nightly royalty run.
Codify AWS infrastructure for the data platform in Terraform modules, with plans reviewed in pull requests before any change reaches production.
Set up GitHub Actions pipelines that run dbt tests and Python unit tests on every merge, blocking broken models before deployment.
Added Great Expectations checks on incoming partner feeds and routed failures to Datadog, giving analysts a clear signal when a late or malformed file would affect the morning dashboards.
Mentor junior engineers through code reviews and pairing on Spark jobs.
Partner with data governance leads to tag sensitive subscriber columns in Snowflake and apply masking policies by role.
Wrote Python utilities that backfill historical viewing data after source corrections.
Reworked the royalty data model with finance after a contract change, adding rights windows and territory rules that kept partner statements accurate from the first payment cycle under the new terms.
employers.stack: Apache Spark, AWS, EMR, Kafka, S3, Snowflake, dbt, Apache Airflow, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Python, Great Expectations, Datadog, data governance

employers.header: Fabrikam Telecom | Data Engineer | Jun 2020 - Jan 2023
employers.usecase: Billing, usage and network data for a regional carrier moved from on-premises Teradata into Snowflake to serve finance, care and network operations reporting. A blended onshore and offshore team ran the migration while month-end close and daily outage reporting continued.
bullets: Migrated billing and usage reporting from an on-premises Teradata warehouse to Snowflake, rebuilding the loads in PySpark and reconciling totals with finance until month-end figures matched.
Built AWS Glue jobs that standardized call detail records from regional switches before they landed in the warehouse.
Applied dimensional modeling to subscriber churn and network quality data, giving care and network teams one shared definition of an active line.
Streamed network alarm events through Kafka into Redshift for near real-time outage dashboards, which let operations staff spot failing cell sites before customer complaints reached the call center.
Scheduled PySpark and SQL jobs in Apache Airflow with dependency checks.
Containerized ingestion jobs with Docker and deployed them through Jenkins CI/CD pipelines that ran unit tests on every build.
Tuned slow Snowflake queries behind the billing dashboards by reworking clustering keys and pruning unused joins.
Published Tableau extracts for churn and usage trends used in quarterly reviews.
Wrote Python validation scripts that compared row counts and revenue totals with source systems after each load, holding back reports when a feed arrived incomplete.
Documented pipeline runbooks, recovery steps and escalation paths in Confluence so the offshore support team could resolve failed loads alone.
Retired legacy Teradata BTEQ scripts after cutover, archiving their logic and outputs for audit and keeping read-only access until finance signed off on a full quarter of Snowflake results.
employers.stack: Teradata, Snowflake, PySpark, AWS Glue, Kafka, Redshift, Apache Airflow, SQL, Docker, Jenkins, CI/CD, Tableau, Python, Confluence, dimensional modeling, runbooks

employers.header: Northwind Systems | Data Engineer | Aug 2018 - May 2020
employers.usecase: A logistics data platform on SQL Server gave planners daily views of shipments, inventory and carrier performance across distribution centers. The role belonged to a small data team supporting operations, finance and procurement users.
bullets: Built Python ETL jobs that loaded shipment, inventory and carrier data into SQL Server for logistics planners.
Moved warehouse scan files from FTP drops to Azure Blob Storage with scheduled ingestion, letting planners see stock levels by early morning instead of waiting for the afternoon batch.
Wrote SQL stored procedures that calculated on-time delivery by carrier.
Developed Power BI reports on fill rates and late shipments, replacing spreadsheets that regional managers rebuilt by hand each week.
Automated daily file checks with Bash and Python, alerting the team when a distribution center missed its upload window.
Introduced Git and Jenkins builds for the ETL code base, giving the team versioned releases and a repeatable path from test to production in place of copying scripts between servers.
Profiled carrier reference data and removed duplicate vendor records before loads.
Collaborated with planners and finance analysts to define inventory metrics and document the source tables behind each one.
Partitioned large shipment history tables in SQL Server, keeping monthly carrier scorecards fast as the data grew.
employers.stack: Python, SQL Server, SQL, Azure, Azure Blob Storage, Power BI, Bash, Git, Jenkins

employers.header: Woodgrove Bank | ETL Developer | Jan 2016 - Jul 2018
employers.usecase: An Oracle reporting warehouse supplied loan, deposit and capital figures to risk and regulatory reporting teams at a retail bank. Releases followed strict change windows, and audit requirements shaped how every load was tested and documented.
bullets: Developed Informatica PowerCenter mappings that loaded loan and deposit data into an Oracle reporting warehouse each night.
Rebuilt the regulatory capital extract with tuned SQL and staged lookups, bringing the overnight batch back inside its window and giving the risk office its numbers before the morning review.
Scheduled batch chains in Control-M with restart points after each stage.
Wrote Unix shell scripts that validated incoming files from upstream banking systems and rejected incomplete deliveries.
Supported quarterly audits by tracing report figures back to source tables and documenting each transformation step.
Masked customer identifiers in test copies of the Oracle warehouse.
Partnered with business analysts to translate regulatory reporting rules into tested mapping specifications, cutting the number of late corrections raised by the finance team at each quarter close.
Converted manual reconciliation spreadsheets into SQL checks that ran after each load and emailed exceptions to the operations desk.
employers.stack: Informatica PowerCenter, Oracle, SQL, Control-M, Unix shell

employers.header: Tailspin Health | Data Analyst | Jun 2014 - Dec 2015
employers.usecase: Claims and member data in SQL Server fed weekly operational reporting for a regional health plan. Early-career tasks centered on reporting, data cleanup and learning the claims process.
bullets: Wrote SQL queries against SQL Server claims tables to produce weekly reports on denial rates and payment delays.
Cleaned member and provider reference data before monthly reporting runs.
Built Excel and SSRS reports for claims operations managers, replacing manual counts with a refreshed view of pending claims by age and payer that supervisors used to plan staffing.
Traced reporting discrepancies to late eligibility files and documented each fix with the data engineers who owned the feeds.
Protected member data by following HIPAA rules for every extract.
Learned Python scripting to automate the weekly report refresh and the row-count checks that ran before it.
Joined weekly meetings with claims supervisors to agree report definitions, refresh timing and the filters each team needed, which cut the follow-up requests that used to arrive after every release.
employers.stack: SQL, SQL Server, Excel, SSRS, Python
